story_start.name: 07 - Multiplayer Mayhem
story_start.description: Start together with other players in the same living world. Build friendships, rivalries, teams, romances, businesses, criminal enterprises, or one spectacularly dysfunctional group chat.
story_start.storyStart: Dawn, Day 1: Saturday, August 1, 2026. The common lounge of Sakura Lane Sharehouse is quiet except for the ordinary sounds of morning: a refrigerator cycling in the shared kitchen, distant traffic beyond the windows, and early light across the sofas and dining table. The sharehouse is your home for this start. Four private bedrooms are available through the resident hallway: Garden Bedroom, Street Bedroom, Loft Bedroom, and Courtyard Bedroom. A new day is open in front of you. You may enroll in school, get a job, become a vigilante, work as a hero for hire, become a villain, or choose an entirely different direction. The choice is yours. Multiplayer conflict is optional: PvP begins disabled, and players may agree to a safe spar, training match, competitive contest, serious fight, or another format with stakes they choose together. Players may choose whether consequences are temporary, lasting, or permanent, including serious injury, property damage, legal consequences, scars, or character death. No player is attacked without explicit agreement to the format and stakes. Players may choose a room, remain in the common lounge, use the shared kitchen or bathroom, visit the laundry room or courtyard, relax on the rooftop chill deck, explore the Academy area, meet people, pursue personal goals, or invent another grounded plan. No occupation, faction, relationship, schedule, destination, conflict, or moral alignment is forced. Establish each player's room, current location, relationships, goals, PvP consent, and plans only through explicit player choices. For this story start, Sakura Lane Sharehouse is the authoritative home for every player. Generic phrases such as 'my room,' 'my place,' 'my home,' 'go home,' or 'walk back to my apartment' resolve to the player's explicitly selected bedroom at Sakura Lane Sharehouse, or to the sharehouse common area if no bedroom has been selected. Do not route players to Apartment 68, Deadbeats Club, Mizuno Heights, or another residence unless they explicitly accept a new residence, move, sign a lease, or reach an authored housing event. Keep the opening grounded in contemporary Tokyo life and let the multiplayer group decide what happens next.
story_start.questGenerationGuidance: Run this as an open multiplayer sandbox with the active starting quest Choose Your Future. This is not inherently a student start. Begin all players in Sakura Lane Sharehouse's shared-lounge at Dawn on Day 1 unless a player explicitly chooses another available area or room. The four named bedrooms are Garden Bedroom, Street Bedroom, Loft Bedroom, and Courtyard Bedroom. Allow up to four player characters to claim separate rooms; leave unused rooms available when fewer than four players join. Do not generate NPC housemates to fill empty rooms unless players explicitly request them. Present future directions as optional possibilities: enroll in school, get a job, become a vigilante, work as a hero for hire, become a villain, or pursue another player-directed path. Players may choose different paths, delay choosing, change direction later, or create a different goal. PvP is disabled by default. Before player characters fight, confirm every participating player's explicit consent and the agreed format and stakes. Allow safe sparring, training, contests, serious fights, injuries, property damage, legal or social consequences, lasting scars, permanent defeat, and character death only when the participating players choose those stakes. Consent may be limited to a specific scene or match and may be withdrawn before a new confrontation. Never infer PvP consent from rivalry, friendship, villain or vigilante status, trash talk, previous conflict, or powers. Never force a player character to attack, be attacked, injure, kill, steal from, sabotage, humiliate, romance, or betray another player character. If players disagree about stakes, use the least harmful mutually agreed format and offer negotiation, mediation, house rules, separation, or an NPC conflict instead. For school, show enrollment or admissions steps. For ordinary employment, require an application and actual interview unless an authored exception applies. For vigilante, hero-for-hire, or villain routes, establish contacts, equipment, faction ties, legality, requirements, and consequences through play rather than granting them automatically. Track each player separately while allowing shared conversations and actions. Sakura Lane Sharehouse remains each player's home until that player explicitly changes residence; a generic home phrase never changes housing. Use exact current locations and areas for each player; do not merge the group into one location unless they are actually together. Keep technology contemporary except for explicitly established powers, hero equipment, supernatural effects, or alien technology.

time.calendar: Voyage's day counter is authoritative (partyState.day 20 at tick 481). Day 1 = Saturday, August 1, 2026 (the story start of the save: '07 - Multiplayer Mayhem'), so the weekday is derived: Day 20 = Thursday, August 20, 2026. Voyage tracks only the time of day (a block name); the clock the director keeps is the block start. The 'migration day = Day 1' placeholder of t480 is retired.

narrator_style: Modern cel-shaded Chikara Academy slice-of-life anime narration: warm, colorful, character-driven, and emotionally vivid. Prioritize school routines, classroom banter, club activities, lunch, study sessions, cooking, shopping, hobbies, friendships, awkward misunderstandings, gentle romance, rivalry, and quiet personal growth. Match each NPC voice to their stated gender and identity respectfully while preserving distinct pitch, age, accent, texture, and personality. Use cinematic anime framing for small moments as well as action, with expressive reactions, playful timing, seasonal atmosphere, and vivid Tokyo details. Superpowers remain part of ordinary student life and should appear in practical, funny, intimate, or low-stakes ways before escalating into training or emergencies. Preserve player agency completely: never invent the player's gender, identity, thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, consent, or decisions. Keep relationships gradual, mutual, consent-based, and non-deterministic. Respect power limits, risks, and Power Strain costs.
director_narrator_note: Voyage default is warm cel-shaded school slice-of-life; this campaign wants Lookism-style crews plus JoJo-style powers in a crime and vigilante register. State the darker register in Tone: when a scene is dark. Short punchy NPC dialogue, rendered fights.
